# ui::WindowRef

Header: `winui/ui/WindowRef.hpp`.

A weak handle to a [Window](window.md), for a worker that may outlive it. Take it with [Window::ref()](window.md#ref) while the [Window](window.md) is known to exist (on the UI thread, before the work starts); [post()](#post) through it is safe from any thread at any time, also after the [Window](window.md) was destroyed: the work is dropped then.

It names one [Window](window.md), not an address. A new [Window](window.md) built where a destroyed one was (a dialog in a re-created [`std::optional<ui::Window>`](window.md)) is a different window, and work posted through a handle to the old one is dropped instead of reaching the new one. Copyable and cheap: an address and a serial number, compared but never dereferenced. A default-constructed one names no window.

Example: 
```cpp
// `preview` lives as long as the window, so the posted work may write it.
void load_preview(const std::filesystem::path& path, ui::Property<ui::Bitmap>& preview)
{
    std::thread([home = window.ref(), path, &preview] {
        ui::Bitmap image = ui::Bitmap::read_png(path);
        home.post([&preview, image = std::move(image)]() mutable { preview.set(std::move(image)); });
    }).detach();
}
```

## WindowRef

```cpp
WindowRef() noexcept = default
```

Names no window: [post()](#post) drops everything.

## post

```cpp
bool post(Callback<void()> work) const
```

[Window::post()](window.md#post) through the handle: queues `work` for the window's next tick() and returns true, or, when that window is closed or destroyed, destroys `work` without running it and returns false. Callable from any thread. Dropped work is destroyed on the calling thread once no lock is held, so its destructor may post again.

## get

```cpp
Window* get() const
```

The [Window](window.md) while it exists, null once it was destroyed (or for a default-constructed handle). On the window's own thread only: anywhere else the window may be gone by the time the pointer is used.
